artists.biography: North Atlantic Oscillation are an electronic rock band based in Scotland.  They released their first single 'Some Blue Hive' on One Records in June 2007. In 2009 the band signed to Kscope - a Snapper Music label - and released an EP called 'Callsigns'. Their debut album 'Grappling Hooks' was released to critical acclaim in the UK in March 2010.  Throughout this period, the band toured the UK and Europe with Porcupine Tree, Anathema and Blackfield.  2012 saw the release of the bands second album, Fog Electric, co-produced by Tony Doogan.  In 2013 the band's vocalist/songwriter Sam Healy released an acclaimed solo album under the name SAND. More info: http://www.sandtheband.com  The band's third album is scheduled for release in late 2014.  Videos: Soft Coda - http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZkAhSSeR8j0 Savage With Barometer - http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nGB_g9w8wuU Drawing Maps From Memory - http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ds63qVri0I  Links: https://www.facebook.com/northatlanticoscillation https://twitter.com/northatlanticos http://www.fogelectric.co.uk http://www.sandtheband.com http://www.kscopemusic.com/northatlanticoscillation/

perplexity.description:
Fog Electric is the second studio album by Scottish trio North Atlantic Oscillation, released in 2012 on the Kscope label. Following their acclaimed debut Grappling Hooks (2010), the band further developed their signature blend of electronic textures and rock dynamics, crafting a sound that sits at the intersection of progressive rock and electro-pop. The album was recorded and produced by Tony Doogan, known for his work with Super Furry Animals, Mogwai, and Belle & Sebastian, lending a polished yet adventurous quality to the music. Fog Electric features a mix of atmospheric electronics, intricate guitar work, and soaring melodies, with recurring themes of contrast and tension—mirroring the meteorological phenomenon referenced in the band’s name.

Musically, Fog Electric is marked by its juxtaposition of dark, brooding tones and expansive, pastoral passages, creating a soundscape that is both dramatic and introspective. The album’s title, drawn from a lyric in the track “Mirador,” reflects its stormy, atmospheric character, with songs that weave together glitchy electronic elements, psychedelic flourishes, and emotive songwriting. Critics praised the album for its inventive production and genre-blurring approach, with outlets like Uncut and Clash highlighting its “intriguing oddness” and “spacious psychedelic rock canvas.” While not a mainstream commercial breakthrough, Fog Electric solidified North Atlantic Oscillation’s reputation as a distinctive voice in the progressive and electronic rock scenes, earning strong critical recognition and a dedicated following.
